candidate_a_iex_sip_bias.evidence: Same-day-only baseline: SIP and IEX block the IDENTICAL 50/77 bars. Cross-session baseline: SIP 55/77 vs IEX 58/77 (+3 bars). Ratio correlation 0.75-0.77 (positive, not 1.0 -- real per-bar noise exists, but feed choice does not flip the outcome).
candidate_a_iex_sip_bias.verdict: NOT the primary driver. Feed choice moves the block count by only ~4-6 percentage points; the block behavior is dominated by the underlying bar-to-bar volume shape of the day, which both feeds largely agree on.

candidate_b_baseline_spans_sessions.evidence: Cross-session baseline (real production mechanism) blocks 55-58/77 (71-75%). Same-day-only baseline (isolating cross-session contamination) blocks 50/77 (64.9%) on BOTH feeds identically. Session-crossing therefore adds ~6-10 percentage points (5-8 extra blocked bars) on top of an already-high 64.9% same-day base rate.
candidate_b_baseline_spans_sessions.verdict: CONFIRMED PRESENT and measurable, but a SECONDARY contributor, not the primary explanation for the day's high block rate. Even a same-day-only baseline already blocks ~65% of bars on 2026-09-02 -- the 0.7x-of-trailing-20-bar threshold is simply strict relative to this day's own volume distribution (a low-turnover drifting move), independent of session-crossing.

cause_analysis.overall: Neither candidate alone explains the magnitude of the block rate. The dominant fact is that on 2026-09-02 most individual 5-min bars traded at LESS than 70% of their own trailing 20-bar average volume -- true under SIP, true under IEX, true with or without the prior-day baseline carryover. Blocker 10 firing 144/178 (tick) or 57/77 (bar) times is consistent with applying the RATIFIED threshold correctly to this day's actual volume shape, not evidence of a computation bug. Session-crossing (b) is a real, present, quantified design property (worth flagging on its own) but did not drive the bulk of the blocking.
